articles.title: India's Stock Exchange Is Going Public: NSE Files for a ₹30,000-Crore IPO, Set to Be the Country's Largest Ever
articles.excerpt: After nearly a decade of regulatory delay, the National Stock Exchange has filed for a pure offer-for-sale of about 6% of its equity — a listing that would hand long-time backers like Azim Premji and Radhakishan Damani a multi-billion-dollar windfall.
articles.image_caption: The National Stock Exchange has filed for a roughly ₹30,000-crore offer-for-sale, set to be India's largest-ever public issue
articles.nri_angle: The exchange where most NRI portfolios are effectively built — through Indian mutual funds, direct equities and the derivatives market — is itself about to list, giving the diaspora both a marquee investment opportunity and a clearer window into how India's market plumbing is valued.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Gold Was Supposed to Soar During the Iran War. It Fell Nearly 10% Instead — Now JP Morgan Sees a 40% Rebound
articles.excerpt: The metal that diaspora families trust as a crisis hedge defied its safe-haven reputation, sliding even as conflict raged, before steadying near ₹1.46 lakh per 10 grams. The episode is a sharp lesson in how gold really behaves — and why timing it is a fool's errand.
articles.image_caption: Gold fell nearly 10% in India during the Iran war despite its safe-haven reputation, before steadying near ₹1.46 lakh per 10 grams
articles.nri_angle: Gold is the diaspora's instinctive store of value — bought for weddings, gifted at festivals, hoarded as insurance against bad times — so its counter-intuitive slide during an actual war, and the debate over where it goes next, speaks directly to how NRIs should size and time their single most emotional investment.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: The RBI Burned Through Nearly $9 Billion in a Single Month Defending the Rupee — and Reserves Are at a One-Year Low
articles.excerpt: Fresh central bank data show the Reserve Bank of India sold a net $8.9 billion in April to slow the rupee's slide, capping a record fiscal year of intervention as foreign reserves fell to $671.6 billion and the currency clawed back from an all-time low.
articles.image_caption: The Reserve Bank of India sold a net $8.9 billion in April to defend the rupee, with forex reserves falling to a one-year low
articles.nri_angle: The scale of the RBI's dollar-selling tells NRIs how hard their central bank is working to keep the rupee from sliding further — a direct signal on the value of remittances, NRE and FCNR deposits, and India-bound investments, and on whether the recent record lows are a floor or a way station.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: The Rupee Just Had Its Best Week in Months. Now a Resurgent Dollar Will Test Whether It Holds.
articles.excerpt: A drop in oil after the US-Iran peace deal pushed the rupee to 94.32, its strongest weekly run in 11 weeks — but a dollar at a one-year high and a hawkish Federal Reserve are pulling the currency back, while government bonds wait on the pace of foreign money returning.
articles.image_caption: The rupee posted its best week in months as oil prices fell, before a resurgent dollar tested the gains
articles.nri_angle: Every move in the rupee reprices the remittances NRIs send home, the value of their NRE and FCNR deposits, and the returns on their Indian investments — so a week that swung from oil-driven relief to dollar-driven pressure is not abstract macro news for the diaspora but a direct signal on when to send money and what their India holdings are worth.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Ambani's Jio Files for What Could Be India's Biggest IPO Ever — and This Time, No One Is Cashing Out
articles.excerpt: Jio Platforms has filed draft papers with India's markets regulator for a fresh-issue-only listing of up to 27 crore shares, a deal market estimates put near ₹36,000 crore at a valuation of roughly ₹12.5 lakh crore — with the proceeds aimed squarely at paying down debt rather than handing existing investors an exit.
articles.image_caption: Reliance Industries chairman Mukesh Ambani, whose Jio Platforms has filed draft papers for a record IPO
articles.nri_angle: Jio touches nearly every Indian family with a phone, and its listing is the marquee event NRI investors have waited years for — a chance to own a slice of the diaspora's most-used digital utility, even as the fresh-issue-only structure and a cooled, war-rattled market raise real questions about price and timing.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: For Once, the Worry Is a Rate Hike: India's Central Bank Holds Steady as War-Driven Oil Tests Its Nerve
articles.excerpt: Minutes of the June meeting show the RBI kept its key rate at 5.25 percent and chose to 'wait and watch' as an Iran-war oil spike sent the rupee tumbling and lifted its inflation forecast to 5.1 percent — even as some economists now bet the next move is up, not down, with HSBC penciling in half a point of hikes this year.
articles.image_caption: The Reserve Bank of India held its key rate at 5.25 percent as a war-driven oil spike clouded the inflation outlook
articles.nri_angle: For NRIs sending money home, parking savings in Indian deposits or holding rupee assets, the prospect of rate hikes rather than cuts flips the usual calculus — it can lift returns on Indian fixed deposits and steady the rupee, but it also signals that war-driven inflation, not growth, is now the force steering India's monetary policy.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Foreigners Keep Selling Indian Stocks. Indians Keep Buying — and That Has Quietly Rewired the Market
articles.excerpt: In May, foreign investors pulled nearly Rs 33,000 crore out of Indian equities while domestic institutions poured in over Rs 82,000 crore — powered by a record Rs 30,954 crore of monthly SIP contributions across 9.64 crore accounts — a structural shift that means the old reflex of watching foreign flows to call the market is increasingly out of date.
articles.image_caption: Domestic mutual fund inflows have grown large enough to absorb foreign investors' selling of Indian equities
articles.nri_angle: Many NRIs still read foreign-investor outflows as a sell signal for Indian stocks, but a steady tide of domestic SIP money is now large enough to absorb that selling — a shift that should reframe how the diaspora thinks about timing, volatility and where the Indian market's real support now comes from.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India Is Dangling Higher Dollar Rates to Pull NRI Money Home — and Banks Now Want to Route It Through GIFT City
articles.excerpt: After the RBI agreed to absorb the hedging cost on fresh foreign-currency NRI deposits and scrapped the rate caps, banks have pushed dollar deposit rates to 6–7 percent and are seeking permission to fund the inflows through their offshore GIFT City units — part of a drive analysts think could draw $55 billion or more to steady the rupee.
articles.image_caption: The Reserve Bank of India has sweetened terms on foreign-currency NRI deposits to draw the diaspora's dollars and steady the rupee
articles.nri_angle: This drive is aimed squarely at the diaspora's wallet: NRIs can suddenly earn 6–7 percent on dollar deposits in Indian banks — nearly double the old rates and with no currency risk — making it one of the most consequential personal-finance shifts for overseas Indians in years.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India Is Courting Foreign Bond Money — but the RBI Wants It Trading at Home, Not Through Euroclear
articles.excerpt: Even after scrapping taxes to lure overseas investors into its government bonds, India's central bank is resisting offshore settlement platforms like Euroclear, insisting foreigners trade directly on the domestic system to keep the market's liquidity in one place.
articles.image_caption: The Reserve Bank of India wants foreign investors to trade its government bonds on the domestic NDS-OM platform rather than via offshore systems
articles.nri_angle: How freely foreign money flows into India's $1-trillion-plus government bond market shapes the rupee, India's borrowing costs and the stability of the assets NRIs hold back home — so the central bank's careful, on-its-own-terms opening of the market is a quiet signal about the financial backdrop against which the diaspora invests, remits and plans for retirement in India.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India's Tax Tribunal Says Money NRIs Send Into Their NRE Accounts From Foreign Salaries Cannot Be Taxed as 'Unexplained' Income
articles.excerpt: An income-tax appellate ruling has deleted a tax demand against a non-resident Indian, holding that once funds in an NRE account are shown to come from foreign earnings, the tax department cannot treat them as unexplained money — a quiet but meaningful protection for the diaspora.
articles.image_caption: India's tax tribunal ruled that foreign-salary credits in an NRI's NRE account cannot be taxed as unexplained income
articles.nri_angle: Millions of NRIs route their overseas salaries into NRE accounts in India to support family, buy property or invest — and the fear of a tax notice questioning those inflows is real, so a tribunal confirming that genuinely foreign-earned money parked in an NRE account is not taxable removes a recurring anxiety for the diaspora.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India's IT Giants Just Hit a Three-Year Low — and a Warning From Accenture Lit the Fuse
articles.excerpt: Infosys, TCS, Wipro and HCLTech tumbled as the Nifty IT index slid to its lowest in three years, after Accenture flagged cautious client spending and a $400 million hit from the Middle East — a chill that runs straight through the diaspora's most familiar industry.
articles.image_caption: India's Nifty IT index fell to a three-year low as Infosys, TCS, Wipro and HCLTech slid after a cautious outlook from Accenture
articles.nri_angle: Indian IT is the diaspora's home turf — it built the careers, H-1B visas and green cards of a huge share of NRIs in the United States, and its shares are a staple of NRI portfolios — so a slump driven by cautious global tech spending is both a portfolio question and a livelihood question for hundreds of thousands of Indian-origin tech workers abroad.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India's Biggest Stock Exchange Is Finally Going Public — in What Could Be the Country's Largest IPO Ever
articles.excerpt: After a decade of delays, the National Stock Exchange has filed papers for a roughly Rs 30,000 crore ($3.3 billion) listing — a pure sale of existing shares that could value the bourse near Rs 5 lakh crore and hand its long-locked-in investors a multi-billion-dollar windfall.
articles.image_caption: The National Stock Exchange has filed for what could be India's largest-ever IPO, a roughly Rs 30,000 crore offer for sale
articles.nri_angle: The NSE is the exchange on which most of the Indian shares and funds that NRIs own actually trade, so its own market debut — potentially India's largest ever — is both a marquee investment opportunity for diaspora portfolios and a barometer of how much appetite global money still has for Indian equities after a bruising year of outflows.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Gold Is Supposed to Soar When the World Looks Dangerous. This Year It Is Doing the Opposite.
articles.excerpt: Bullion has logged its sixth straight week of lower or flat closes and is grinding toward $4,000 — far below February's near-$5,600 record — even with a Middle East war and an unsigned ceasefire on the table. The reason is not fear, but a hawkish Federal Reserve and a dollar at a 13-month high.
articles.image_caption: Gold has logged six straight weeks of lower or flat closes, sliding toward $4,000 amid a hawkish Fed
articles.nri_angle: Gold is the diaspora's default store of value — in wedding jewellery, in sovereign gold bonds, in the ETFs and coins NRIs buy to hedge a wobbly rupee — so a sharp, counter-intuitive slide in the metal even as geopolitical risk lingers is a direct signal to Indian-origin investors about whether their favourite safe haven is still doing the job they bought it for.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India's Central Bank Holds Rates and Trims Its Growth Forecast as the West Asia War Clouds the Outlook
articles.excerpt: Minutes from the Reserve Bank of India's June meeting show a rate panel content to wait and watch — holding the repo rate at 5.25 percent while cutting the FY27 growth forecast to 6.6 percent, as the conflict in West Asia muddies the trade-off between inflation and growth.
articles.image_caption: The RBI held its repo rate at 5.25 percent and cut its FY27 growth forecast to 6.6 percent in June
articles.nri_angle: The RBI's growth and inflation calls shape everything NRIs care about back home — the value of the rupee against their salaries abroad, the returns on their Indian deposits and equities, and the cost of money for family and businesses in India — so the central bank's cautious posture and lowered growth forecast are a direct read on the climate for diaspora money.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: After a Record Exodus, Foreign Investors Tiptoed Back Into Indian Stocks This Week
articles.excerpt: Foreign portfolio investors bought a net ₹1,209 crore of Indian equities in the week to June 20 — a small but symbolically important turn after dumping a record $30 billion-plus through 2026, as a US-Iran peace deal and cheaper oil revived appetite for emerging markets.
articles.image_caption: Foreign investors turned net buyers of Indian equities in the week to June 20 after a record 2026 sell-off
articles.nri_angle: Many NRIs hold Indian equities directly or through mutual funds and India-focused ETFs abroad, so a tentative reversal in foreign flows — the single biggest swing factor for Indian stocks this year — matters directly to diaspora portfolios and to anyone weighing whether the worst of 2026's sell-off is behind them.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Foreign Money Fled India in April, but a Record Surge in NRI Remittances Helped Cushion the Blow
articles.excerpt: India's balance of payments slipped into a $6.6 billion deficit as portfolio investors pulled out, yet net transfers from overseas Indians jumped to $16 billion — and the RBI's push to draw NRI dollars may turn the tide next year.
articles.image_caption: India's balance of payments slipped into deficit in April even as NRI remittances surged to a record $16 billion
articles.nri_angle: This is the diaspora's economic footprint laid bare: as foreign funds fled Indian stocks, it was the money sent home by Indians working abroad — a record $16 billion in a single month — that helped steady the national accounts, underscoring how central NRIs have become to India's financial stability.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Jio Files for India's Biggest-Ever IPO — and for the First Time, the Diaspora Can Own a Piece of It
articles.excerpt: Mukesh Ambani's Jio Platforms has filed papers for a Mumbai listing aiming to raise around $3.8 billion, eclipsing every IPO India has seen. For NRIs who use Jio to call home, the company they rely on is about to become one they can invest in.
articles.image_caption: The Bombay Stock Exchange in Mumbai; Jio Platforms has filed for what would be India’s largest-ever IPO, aiming to raise around $3.8 billion
articles.nri_angle: Jio is the invisible infrastructure of diaspora life — the SIM in a parent's phone, the data behind every video call home, the connection that keeps NRI families tethered to India. Now the company behind it is filing for the country's largest-ever IPO, turning a service the diaspora depends on into an asset it can, for the first time, actually own a share of.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk
